supremeCourt.name: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF)
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Nominated by the President, confirmed by the Senate; mandatory retirement at 75.
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: No structural change to the court. PT presidents (Lula, Dilma) filled vacancies through the normal process. As of 2026 a majority of the 11 sitting justices were appointed by PT (FSP) presidents: Lula appointed Cármen Lúcia, Dias Toffoli, Cristiano Zanin and Flávio Dino (with Jorge Messias nominated for the seat vacated by Barroso's 2025 retirement); Dilma appointed Luiz Fux and Edson Fachin (the current court president). The rest were appointed by FHC (Gilmar Mendes), Temer (Alexandre de Moraes) and Bolsonaro (Nunes Marques, André Mendonça).
supremeCourt.stillServing: About 7 of the 11 current justices were appointed by FSP (PT) presidents Lula and Dilma — a working majority — as of 2026 (snapshot; the Barroso-seat confirmation was still in process).

courtHistory.event: STF created (Decreto 848/1890; confirmed by the 1891 Constitution) with 15 ministers, replacing the imperial Supremo Tribunal de Justiça.
Decreto 19.656, an act of Getúlio Vargas's Provisional Government, reduced the court from 15 to 11 ministers (and retired several).
Estado Novo dictatorship: Vargas pressured and reshaped the court; judicial review was curtailed under the 1937 charter.
Ato Institucional nº 2 (AI-2) expanded the court from 11 to 16 ministers, letting the military regime appoint a majority.
Under AI-5 the regime forcibly retired three ministers (Hermes Lima, Victor Nunes Leal and Evandro Lins e Silva); AI-6 then returned the court to 11 seats — the size it keeps today.
The new democratic Constitution kept 11 ministers and set mandatory retirement at 70.
Constitutional Amendment 88 ('PEC da Bengala') raised mandatory retirement from 70 to 75, slowing turnover on the court.
No structural change; vacancies filled through the normal appointment process. By 2026 about 7 of the 11 justices had been appointed by PT (FSP) presidents — see the current-bench table below.
